records.c: Save A, X and Y; inspect the stacked status and dispatch BRK through $0316 or IRQ through $0314.

Six 64-byte sprite slots in VIC bank 0, used in the equipment-panel frame. A slot holds 63 shape bytes and one trailing byte. The frame's sprite pointers select shapes from this range; which object each shape represents remains open.
Primary screen data, bytes 0–255 of 1,000. Museum setup at $8396 copies this portion.
Primary screen data, bytes 256–511 of 1,000. Museum setup at $8396 copies this portion.

One thousand colour-matrix bytes copied to $0400-$07E7 by the equipment-panel setup at $CAA8. In the panel's multicolour bitmap display each byte supplies two colours for one character-sized cell.
Equipment-panel colour-matrix bytes $1900-$19FF; $CAA8 copies them to the corresponding portion of the screen at $0400.
Equipment-panel colour-matrix bytes $1A00-$1AFF; $CAA8 copies them to the corresponding portion of the screen at $0400.

Eight thousand bitmap bytes read by the VIC in the equipment-panel frame. The panel interrupt selects VIC bank 0 and multicolour bitmap mode with the bitmap at $2000; the frame rebuilt from this memory and the register writes matches the captured VICE image pixel for pixel. Other uses of the same bytes remain open.
Equipment-panel multicolour bitmap bytes $2400-$27FF; this is the continuation of the 8,000-byte bitmap at $2000, read by the VIC in bank 0.
Equipment-panel multicolour bitmap bytes $2800-$2BFF; this is the continuation of the 8,000-byte bitmap at $2000, read by the VIC in bank 0.

Equipment-panel multicolour bitmap bytes $3C00-$3F3F; this is the continuation of the 8,000-byte bitmap at $2000, read by the VIC in bank 0.

Sixty-three sprite bitmap bytes selected by pointer $7C. In the captured floor VIC bank, this pointer addresses $5F00. The moving object's identity remains open.

First 128 eight-byte glyphs of the museum character set at $7000. The captured floor scene selects this base in VIC bank 1; the bytes are identical in the entry, rope and floor snapshots. Other uses of this memory need checking.

Last 128 eight-byte glyphs of the museum character set at $7000. The captured floor scene selects this base in VIC bank 1; the bytes are identical in the entry, rope and floor snapshots. Other uses of this memory need checking.
First 128 eight-byte glyphs of the alternate museum character set, selected by $D018 value $1F in the alternate screen setup.
Last 128 eight-byte glyphs of the alternate museum character set at $7800.
If $9485 is nonzero, call $9981 only when $804D equals $8041, then return. Otherwise return outside room 1; in room 1 continue to the three-by-three screen update at $8301.
When $8046 is nonzero, copy the first three codes of each four-byte row at $8372, $8376 and $837A into the three screen rows at $45F6, $461E and $4646. Otherwise continue at $8320.
Increment $8044 and return unless it reaches six. Then clear it, increment $8045. When it reaches two, clear $8045 and choose the pattern at $833E; otherwise choose the pattern at $8358.
Copy the first three codes of each four-byte row at $837E, $8382 and $8386 to $45F6, $461E and $4646, then return.
Copy the first three codes of each four-byte row at $838A, $838E and $8392 to $45F6, $461E and $4646, then return.
Frame 0, row 1: four character codes; the animation routine at $82E8 copies the first three into the portrait-room screen.
Frame 0, row 2: four character codes; the animation routine at $82E8 copies the first three into the portrait-room screen.
Frame 0, row 3: four character codes; the animation routine at $82E8 copies the first three into the portrait-room screen.
Frame 1, row 1: four character codes; the animation routine at $82E8 copies the first three into the portrait-room screen.
Frame 1, row 2: four character codes; the animation routine at $82E8 copies the first three into the portrait-room screen.

Frame 2, row 2: four character codes; the animation routine at $82E8 copies the first three into the portrait-room screen.
Frame 2, row 3: four character codes; the animation routine at $82E8 copies the first three into the portrait-room screen.

If $8041 is zero, set the display-memory operand at $087B to $1D, copy 1,000 screen codes from $1000 to $4400 and the low nibbles of 1,000 bytes at $1C00 to colour RAM, then call $82E8. Otherwise continue at $83DE.

Set the display-memory operand at $087B to $1F, call $A36A for the upper screen, copy 488 further codes from $1600 to $4600, and copy the high nibbles of 1,000 bytes at $1C00 to colour RAM before calling $82E8.
Eight bytes added to the low X position at $FC05 by $FE30 after selecting a direction. The result and carry are stored at $FE12/$FE13.
Eight bytes added to the Y position at $FC15 by $FE30 after selecting a direction. The routine subtracts 8 and stores the result at $FE14.
Add 8 to the byte at $8049 and return. The placement routine calls this twice when its computed row is below 6.

Save Y on the stack, set $99C1 to 3 and copy $804A,X to $804D. Read $FC16,Y into $8049, substituting $D2 for $CF, $D0 or $D1; copy $FC06,Y/$FC0E,Y to $8047/$8048 and subtract $10. Subtract $0C from that two-byte value and shift its low byte right three places. Subtract $32 from $8049, shift right three, and round an even result up to an odd value; when it is below 6, add 2 and advance $8049 by 16. Use the row value to select a word at $8428, add the shifted position and, if the adjusted position's high byte is nonzero, $20. Save this address at $99C6/$99C7 and its value plus $28 at $99CC/$99CD. Patch the reads at $97E9 and $9835 to this address. Read the byte at offset 4 and, depending on $8041, test it against $C4, $C5, $D8 and $D9 or against $A9 before continuing at $9835.

High byte of the self-modified read at $9835; $97E3 sets it from the calculated address. The read byte goes to $9488 and selects calls to $9664 and $9698 for $39–$3B. The value of $8041 selects one of two further groups of comparisons against $9488, with calls to $9664, $9698, $99D2 and $99D9; both paths continue at $9958. The meanings of the tested cell codes remain open.

Set $947F to 4 and use that index to copy values from $CA95 and $CA9A to $CA88 and $CA8E. Set $9486,X to 1, restore the saved Y, preserve X across a call to $963F, clear $947E and set $9485 to 1. Execution then falls into $9981.

Copy four bytes each from $99E8 and $99EC to the working rows at $99E0 and $99E4. If $8041 is zero and the destination at $99C6/$99C7 equals $4518, change the first working byte to $81; if it equals $44E4, change the fourth to $A2. Copy the working rows through the self-modified stores at $99C5 and $99CB, whose operands are set by $97DA–$97E6 and $97C4–$97D2. The immediate operand at $99C1 determines the descending index: $96F8 sets it to 3 and some cell tests set it to 1.
If $9486 is nonzero, clear it and return. Otherwise toggle $948A. When setting it, call $871B; when clearing it, call $FE96 if $FE19 is nonzero. The gameplay role of $948A remains open.

If $FE19 is nonzero, call $FE96, then process one movement slot through $9B5A. Index $C00C with $8026. While that byte is nonzero, increment $94DA and clear both when the counter reaches $D0, then return. Otherwise read bit $10 of CIA1 port A, the joystick-2 fire line. A set bit clears the latch at $9489; a clear bit with the latch already set returns. On a newly detected clear bit, set the latch, call $9656 or $956C according to $947E/$947F, then call $9A71 to initialize a free movement slot. The exact gameplay identity of the moving object remains open.

If $9486 is nonzero, clear it and return. Otherwise select the first zero flag among $949D–$949F; if none is zero, return. Call $86E1 with A=$0D and call $C02C, set the selected flag to 1, and call $FE30. Save the direction at $FE18 into the selected byte at $94A0–$94A2. Copy the position at $FE12–$FE14 into the selected three-byte slot at $948F–$9497, subtracting $10 from its low/high pair when the direction is at least 5. The exact gameplay identity of the slot remains open.

Increment the counter at $949C. If it becomes three, reset it to zero and process slot 0 at $9B96; if it becomes one, process slot 1 at $9BD1; otherwise process slot 2 at $9C0C. The routine processes one slot per call.

With X=0, call $9E18 and $9EB4, then call $9F52 with Y=2, then run the direction dispatcher at $9C47 with X=0. The callers first load the selected slot into the shared state at $9498–$949B and copy the updated position back afterward.
Write $03 to $FC2B and return. The three slot handlers jump here when their respective active byte is zero.

If $949D is zero, write $03 to $FC2B and return. Otherwise copy direction $94A0 and position $948F–$9491 into $9498–$949B, select flag index 0 in $94A3, and call $9B79. Copy the updated position back to $948F–$9491.

If $949E is zero, write $03 to $FC2B and return. Otherwise copy direction $94A1 and position $9492–$9494 into $9498–$949B, select flag index 1 in $94A3, and call $9B79. Copy the updated position back to $9492–$9494.

If $949F is zero, write $03 to $FC2B and return. Otherwise copy direction $94A2 and position $9495–$9497 into $9498–$949B, select flag index 2 in $94A3, and call $9B79. Copy the updated position back to $9495–$9497.

Read the direction selector at $9498 and jump to one of eight handlers for values 0 through 7; return without a handler for any other value. Each handler first calls $9C81, chooses a byte at $FC2B,X and then updates the position state at $9499–$949B.

Copy the three state bytes at $9499, $949A and $949B to $FC0B,X, $FC13,X and $FC1B,X, respectively. The caller chooses X. This runs before each directional update, so these destinations receive the previous state.

If X is 1, clear $94B2,Y with Y taken from $94B8; for any other X clear $949D,Y with Y taken from $94A3. The direction handlers call this when their position crosses a boundary. The gameplay identities of these arrays remain open.
Publish the prior position, set $FC2B,X to $7C, and subtract 10 from $949B. If the resulting byte is below $28, call $9C94 to clear the selected flag.

Publish the prior position, set $FC2B,X to $7D, and add 10 to the little-endian value at $9499/$949A. If the high byte is nonzero and the low byte is at least $60, clear the selected flag; otherwise subtract 5 from $949B and clear the flag if that result is below $28.
Publish the prior position, set $FC2B,X to $7E, and add 10 to the little-endian value at $9499/$949A. If the high byte is nonzero and the low byte is at least $60, clear the selected flag.

Publish the prior position, set $FC2B,X to $7F, and add 10 to the little-endian value at $9499/$949A. If the high byte is nonzero and the low byte is at least $60, clear the selected flag; otherwise add 5 to $949B and clear the flag if that result is at least $EA.
Publish the prior position, set $FC2B,X to $80, and add 10 to $949B. If the resulting byte is at least $EA, clear the selected flag.

Publish the prior position, set $FC2B,X to $81, and subtract 10 from the little-endian value at $9499/$949A. If the high byte is zero and the low byte is below $10, clear the selected flag; otherwise add 5 to $949B and clear the flag if that result is at least $EA.
Publish the prior position, set $FC2B,X to $82, and subtract 10 from the little-endian value at $9499/$949A. If the high byte is zero and the low byte is below $10, clear the selected flag.

Publish the prior position, set $FC2B,X to $83, and subtract 10 from the little-endian value at $9499/$949A. If the high byte is zero and the low byte is below $10, clear the selected flag; otherwise subtract 5 from $949B and clear the flag if that result is below $28.

Subtract $0C from the two-byte position at $9499/$949A and $32 from $949B. Shift the low-byte results right by three and use the latter to select a word from $8428; combine that word with the shifted first value and the high-byte and $804A,X conditions to patch the address operand at $9E95/$9E96. Read the resulting address at $9E94. If the byte is 1, clear the selected flag in $949D,Y or $94B2,Y according to X. The row table's content and the meaning of value 1 remain open.

Return immediately if $A2F9 or $8050 is nonzero, or if $804A,X differs from $804C. Otherwise form half-width horizontal values from $9499/$949A and $FC09/$FC11, then require the first plus 3 to be at least the second and less than the second plus 7. Also require $949B to be at least $FC19+6 and less than $FC19+$11, using byte arithmetic. On a match clear the selected flag in $949D,Y or $94B2,Y according to X, then call $A474. The identity of the compared objects remains open.

Return if $8027 equals 4 for X other than 1, or if $8026 equals 4 for X=1. Also return unless $804A equals $804B. Form half-width horizontal values from $9499/$949A and $FC05,Y/$FC0D,Y; require the first plus 3 to be at least the second and less than the second plus 7. Require $949B to be at least $FC15,Y+6 and less than $FC15,Y+$11, using byte arithmetic. On a match, X=1 clears the selected $94B2 flag and calls $C33D; other values clear the selected $949D flag and call $C35D. The gameplay identity of these compared objects remains open.

Index $CA8F with $8026. Unless the result is $3D, clear $948A. If $948A remains nonzero call $871B; otherwise, when the indexed value is not $3C, clear the three flags at $949D–$949F and write $03 to $FC2B, then call the three-slot cycle at $9B5A. Next index $CA8F with $8027. When that byte is $3D, optionally call $8DC2 according to $948D and inspect bit $10 of $DC00. A newly detected clear bit sets $948C, chooses $965D or $9573 according to $947E/$947F, clears $C00C indexed by $8027, and calls $A080. A set bit clears $948C; a held clear bit returns. Other values branch to $A0A7.
If $A2D8 is zero, copy 512 codes from $1400 to $4400 and return. Otherwise follow the partial-copy and patch path at $A381.
Copy selected ranges from the alternate screen to $4400–$45FF, then repeat six bytes from $A364 in eight screen rows. This is the nonzero-$A2D8 branch of $A36A.

Increment the counter at $A2F7. When it reaches 5, clear it and increment $A2F8. For $A2F8 values 1 through 4, use it as an index into $C674 and $C679 and write the results to $FC29 and $8018. When $A2F8 reaches 5, jump to the congratulations path at $0A16 if $8050 equals 2; otherwise clear $A2F8, set $8050 to 2, copy 63 bytes from $4280 to $6500 and update the associated pointers. The meaning and normal triggers of these phases need further tracing.

Scan keyboard matrix rows, including Space. When $8028 is zero, a new Space press toggles $8042 between 0 and 1, calls $86B6 with the selected entry from $8026/$8027 and may call $8396. It then selects the corresponding offsets in $B356 and $B357 and continues to joystick movement at $B459. The earlier key scans can divert or wait before reaching that point.

Read joystick port 2 into $803F and select directional movement. Up takes precedence over down; within either vertical path left takes precedence over right. With neither vertical direction, left takes precedence over right. The selected path writes values to $FC25/$FC26 indexed by $B356, calls movement helpers and advances a four-update animation counter at $8040; the animation's next value is kept in the immediate operand of the path's load instruction.

If room $8041 is zero, stop when the high X byte $FC0F is zero and the low byte $FC07 is below $20; otherwise subtract two from the 16-bit X value and copy it to $FC08/$FC10. In a nonzero room, use the crossing check at $BEA5.
If the high X byte $FC0F is zero and the low byte $FC07 is below $25, change to room zero at $BEB1; otherwise subtract two at $BECD.
Set $8041 and $804B to zero, set both low X bytes $FC07/$FC08 to $10 and both high bytes $FC0F/$FC10 to 1, and call screen setup at $8396.
Subtract two from the 16-bit X value at $FC07/$FC0F, duplicate it at $FC08/$FC10, and return.

When $8041 is zero, check the high byte at $FC0F and low byte at $FC07. If the high byte is nonzero and the low byte is at least $3A, take the room-change path at $BFB2; otherwise advance at $BFCE. When $8041 is nonzero, use the limit check at $BFE6.
Set the current and second character's room bytes $8041 and $804B to 1, set both low X bytes at $FC07–$FC08 to $40 and both high bytes at $FC0F–$FC10 to zero, then call the screen setup at $8396.
Add two to the 16-bit X value at $FC07/$FC0F, duplicate the resulting low and high bytes at $FC08 and $FC10, and return.
If $FC0F is nonzero and $FC07 is at least $40, return without moving. Otherwise add two to $FC07/$FC0F, duplicate the resulting bytes at $FC08/$FC10, and return.

Read the value at $8026. Values 0, 1, 2 and 3 jump to $C376, $C42B, $C4E0 and $C595 respectively; any other value returns. The indexed overlap check at $9F52 calls this path when X=1 and its position tests match.

Read the value at $8027. Values 1, 2 and 3 jump to $C42B, $C4E0 and $C595 respectively; any other value returns. The indexed overlap check at $9F52 calls this path when X is not 1 and its position tests match.

Examine the low byte of the load operand at $C384. If it is $FC, set $C319 to 1 and return. Otherwise copy one byte through the self-modified load at $C383 and store at $C386, initially $42C0 to $6340. Add 3 to both operands. Set the reverse load operand at $C3E1/$C3E2 to the new source operand minus $3D, and add 3 to the reverse store operand at $C3E4/$C3E5. Return. The effect of the copied pattern in play remains open.

If the low byte of the reverse load operand at $C3E1 is $80, clear $C31D and return. Otherwise set $C31D to 1, copy one byte through the patched load at $C3E0 and store at $C3E3, subtract 3 from the forward load operand at $C384/$C385, set the reverse load operand to that updated value minus $3D, and subtract 3 from the forward and reverse store operands at $C387/$C388 and $C3E4/$C3E5.
Advance the descent, then read joystick port 2. Up decreases $8058 unless it is zero; otherwise down increases it while it is below 7. If both are held, the up path takes precedence.

For the player indexed by $C672, add $8058 to both position bytes at $FC15 and $FC16 while the first is below $B0. Every fourth such update, increase a nonzero $8058 unless it is 8. When the first position reaches $B0 or more, set $805B to 1.

Set up the four-character panel: switch the raster interrupt, copy screen bytes from $1800-$1BE7 to $0400-$07E7 and fill the corresponding colour RAM with $0F. The loop waits for the interrupt-updated $CAA4 to change, then calls $CCDC. When $CAA6 is set, it clears that flag and returns to the museum floor via $81A9.

Set VIC bank 0 and multicolour bitmap mode, call the sound update at $E13A and configure eight sprites for the upper panel row. Install $CC10 as the next raster interrupt at line $DA and leave through $0867. Several sprite pointers in this routine are immediate operands changed by the panel setup.

Configure six multicolour sprites for the panel's lower row, call $CC4A to position them and process panel input, increment the main loop's $CAA4 counter, then install $CB76 as the next interrupt at line 0 and leave through $0867.

Copy the six 9-bit horizontal positions from $CA83-$CA8E into the sprite X registers and $D010, set their Y positions to $E0, and copy $CA94 and $CA8F-$CA93 to sprite pointers $07F8-$07FD. Execution falls through to $CCDC, which reads the panel controls before returning to the interrupt handler.

Read joystick port 2 into $CAA5. A new fire press calls $CD88, which dispatches to four cursor-position-dependent handlers; left and right call the cursor adjustment routines $CD62 and $CD74 within their bounds. When $CA94 is $3E, Space may set $CAA6 after it is released; another exit path depends on fire and cursor state.

Handle fire in the first slot cursor region, where $CA89 is zero and $CA83 is below $45. With $CA94 equal to $3E, copy the slot value at $CA8F into $CA94 and write $3F to the slot. Otherwise return $3E to $CA94 and use the offset at $CD87 to exchange the held and slot values.

Use A to select a seven-byte record at $EB5C: one accumulator increment and three little-endian pointers. Clear the three $24-byte channel state blocks, initialize their pointers and counters from the selected record, clear SID registers, and enable the channel update flags.
Call the three-voice SID update at $E141, then call the separate routine at $E937 before returning.

If $E12E is nonzero, advance an eight-bit accumulator; on carry call $E3A3 for channel offsets $00, $24 and $48, then call $E43D for all three. For each enabled channel, write its stored frequency, pulse width, envelope and control values to the SID; finally write $E138 to $D418.
Immediate operand of the LDA at $E146. Initialization copies the selected record's first byte here; each enabled sound update adds it to the accumulator stored in the operand at $E14A.

Immediate operand of the ADC at $E149 and the accumulator for the sound update. Initialization writes $FF here; the update stores each sum back. Carry from the addition controls whether it advances the three channel streams.
Entry 0 in the little-endian command jump table at $E226 holds $E2B1. The dispatcher at $E42C reads an indexed pair from this table.
Entry 1 in the little-endian command jump table at $E226 holds $E392. The dispatcher at $E42C reads an indexed pair from this table.
Entry 2 in the little-endian command jump table at $E226 holds $E38B. The dispatcher at $E42C reads an indexed pair from this table.
Entry 3 in the little-endian command jump table at $E226 holds $0000. The dispatcher at $E42C reads an indexed pair from this table.

Read a two-byte sequence-table base from the stream into indexed voice state, then select the first pointer in that table.

Add the indexed voice's offset to its sequence-table base and advance the offset. If the selected two-byte pointer is zero, reset to the first table entry; load the selected pointer into the stream pointer and continue reading.
Copy three bytes from the sound stream into indexed voice state at $E0DF-$E0E1, advance the stream pointer by three, set $E0E2 to one, and continue reading commands.

Clear two indexed voice state bytes, take the next stream byte into $E0D9, advance the pointer and continue reading commands.

Set bit $20 in the indexed voice's $E0C2 state, clear $E0C9 and $E0CA, and copy three stream bytes to $E0CE-$E0D0. The $E341 entry sets bit $04 instead. Both advance the pointer by three and continue reading.

Clear the indexed voice's $E0DE state and continue reading the stream.
Set the low two bits of the indexed voice's $E0C2 state and continue reading the stream.

Count down the indexed voice's delay. When it expires, read its byte stream: values below $80 set the next value and reload the delay, $80-$BF dispatch through the command table, and higher values change stream parameters before reading again. Save the advanced pointer when a value is accepted.

For the channel selected by X, read a byte from the stream addressed by $E0CB/$E0CC plus $E0CD. A byte with bit 7 set resets the stream offset to $FF and has that bit cleared. Add $E0D3, the global offset at $E464 and $E0E5; use the result to select a little-endian frequency from $E5C2. The continuation at $E464 applies the channel's optional frequency and pulse adjustments and stores the resulting SID values in its state block.

Immediate operand of the ADC at $E463. Initialization clears it; a sound-stream command at $E2C7 replaces it. The same routine then adds the channel byte at $E0E5, looks up a two-byte frequency and applies enabled pitch and pulse-width adjustments before storing the channel's frequency at $E0D6/$E0D7 and pulse width at $E0D8/$E0D9.

Update the shared modulation state, then call each active voice's effect routine according to the three flags at $E12F-$E131.

Update the first voice's timed effect. When its remaining count reaches zero, clear its active flag and envelope registers and set its completion flag. Otherwise count down the effect, periodically reload its frequency and add or subtract its configured frequency step before writing SID voice 1.
Update the second voice's timed effect: clear its flag and envelope on expiry, otherwise count down, reload and step its frequency and write SID voice 2.
Update the third voice's timed effect: clear its flag and envelope on expiry, otherwise count down, reload and step its frequency and write SID voice 3.
